newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan minister-budget deficit 3.9 pct of GDP '97.
newsitem.headline: Jordan minister-budget deficit 3.9 pct of GDP '97.

text.p: Finance Minister Marwan Awad said on Monday that projected state spending would rise 11 percent in 1997 to 1.916 billion dinars ($2.7 billion), leaving a deficit without foreign aid of 3.9 percent of GDP or 225 million dinars.

"The draft budget was prepared to reduce the budget deficit as a percentage of GDP by improving instruments of collecting public revenue and reining in public expenditure and to increase national savings," Awad told reporters.
Total state revenues, including foreign aid of 169 million dinars, were forecast to reach 1.860 billion dinars, up six percent from the 1996 readjusted budget figure, Awad said.
The budget deficit is expected to be a readjusted 237 million dinars in 1996, or 4.6 percent of GDP.
The draft budget, approved with some alterations by Jordan's cabinet on Saturday, reflects accelerated IMF-agreed reforms in 1997-1998. It will be sent to parliament soon for approval.
Awad said he was optimistic that Jordan would be able to reduce its budget deficit by the end of a final third year of expanded IMF-directed reforms in 1998 to 2.5 percent of GDP.
Current expenditure was forecast to rise 8.2 percent in 1997 to 1.481 billion dinars, Awad said.

This includes 72 million dinars allocated for the first time for cash payments in compensation for raising bread prices last August, which sparked the worst civil unrest since 1989. It eliminates a subsidy budget that existed for imports of wheat.

Awad said the 1997 draft budget did not include any new measures for an increase in taxes and tariffs but stressed that a projected 8.2 percent rise in local revenue to 1.691 billion dinars in 1997 would be attained by enhanced tax collection.
